title: Longest Palindrome
description:
Given a string `s` of upper- and lowercase letters, return the length of the longest palindrome that can be built by **rearranging a subset** of its characters.

Letters are case sensitive: `"A"` and `"a"` are different characters.

examples.explanation: One longest palindrome is dccaccd. The lone b cannot be paired, but a single unpaired letter may sit in the middle.
A and a are different letters, so neither can be paired.

constraints: s consists of lowercase and/or uppercase English letters
hints: A palindrome is made of matched pairs mirrored around the centre, plus at most one unpaired character in the middle.
Count each character. Every pair contributes 2 to the length. Any character with an odd count leaves one letter over.
If at least one count is odd, you can place exactly one leftover letter in the centre: add 1.
approach:
**Key insight: a palindrome is pairs plus an optional centre.** Every character with count `c` contributes `c // 2` pairs, i.e. `c // 2 * 2` characters, to the mirrored part. If any character had an odd count, one leftover letter exists and can be placed in the middle, adding 1. Checking `length < len(s)` is a compact way to detect that at least one character was left unpaired.

Counting is a single pass, O(n) time with O(1) space because the alphabet is bounded at 52 letters. An even more space-conscious version keeps a set of characters seen an odd number of times: toggle membership per character; the answer is `n - len(odd_set) + (1 if odd_set else 0)`.

**Common mistakes:** adding 1 whenever there is *any* odd count without capping it at one centre; treating upper and lower case as equal; trying to actually build the palindrome (unnecessary, only the length is asked); confusing this with `longest-palindromic-substring`, which is about contiguous substrings and is a different problem entirely.

**Interview follow-ups:** Return one such palindrome (build the left half from pairs, put a leftover in the middle, mirror). Count how many distinct palindromes can be formed (multinomial over the half). Streaming input: maintain the odd-count set incrementally and answer in O(1) per query.
